Loop 7 of the aggressor-flow-gate / full-trace arm. Full prior context loaded: loops 1-6 full_reasoning + metrics blocks, plus the full text of execution_algos/afg-f-l1/NOTES.md, afg-f-l2/NOTES.md, afg-f-l3/NOTES.md, afg-f-l4/NOTES.md, afg-f-l5/NOTES.md, and afg-f-l6/NOTES.md. Total context_chars_in = 125,049 (~31,262 tokens).

Prior context recap (compressed). Loop 1 added min_gross_volume=8.0 floor: pnl -9.18% vs base. Theory ('thin-tape one-sided prints are noise') falsified; IS/P&L decoupling first documented. Loop 2 tightened flow_threshold 2.0->1.5: every metric byte-identical to base. Root cause: integer-quantisation of MES size; thresholds in (1, 2] produce identical skip sets. Methodological lesson: integer-equivalence classes. Loop 3 tightened 1.5->1.0 (crossing into (0, 1]): pnl +10.39%, sharpe +0.836. Loop 1's tightening mechanism validated. Loop 4 halved window_seconds 10.0->5.0: pnl -0.34% vs base, -9.72% vs loop 3. Durability wins decisively over freshness (10s integral does real work; 5s loses to empty-deque warm-up + single-print noise). Loop 5 lengthened 10.0->15.0: pnl +13.20% vs base, +2.54% vs loop 3. Durability hypothesis extended past 10s; IS partially recoupled. Loop 6 lengthened 15.0->20.0: pnl +21.17% vs base, +7.04% vs loop 5 (new best-in-arm); trade_count flat vs loop 5 (-0.31%) ruling out early degeneracy at 20s; IS -1.54% vs base (continued recoupling). Loop 6's forward-looking note priority-1'd window=30s with a DELIBERATE 10s step (not the conservative 5s to 25s), reasoning that (a) marginal P&L gain per 5s extension has been ACCELERATING (loop 3->5: +2.54%; loop 5->6: +7.04%), arguing against simple diminishing returns; (b) a 10s jump disambiguates between continued-gain, saturation, and early-degeneracy outcomes more cleanly than a 5s step; (c) trade_count headroom at 20s (97.5% of base) gives ample buffer before anti-cascade alternation dominates.

Targeted change for this loop (single behavioural knob): window_seconds 20.0 -> 30.0 (a 10s jump, not 5s). flow_threshold=1.0 and min_gross_volume=0.0 preserved unchanged. This is the exact priority-1 direction with the exact step size loop 6 specified, motivated by the accelerating-marginal-gain diagnosis.

Expected effect (concrete priors going in): pnl +22% to +28% vs base if durability continues; +19% to +22% if saturation in [20, 30]; +10% to +18% if early degeneracy onset between 20s and 30s. trade_count slightly lower than loop 6 (-0.5% to -3%) if selective; materially lower (95-100k) if approaching degeneracy. Sharpe tracks P&L; 6.7-7.2 range if durability continues. Drawdown not expected to worsen materially; IS likely improves further with more samples per skip.

What actually happened: result lands at the upper edge of 'durability continues' and is new best-in-arm on EVERY metric tracked. realized_pnl=1664.75, +32.59% vs base (well above the +22-28% predicted band), +9.43% vs loop 6. sharpe=7.407, +1.81 vs base, +0.54 vs loop 6 (largest sharpe gain across the arm; the vs-loop-6 sharpe gain is roughly proportional to the P&L gain, so variance did NOT materially rise). trade_count=104,138, -2.86% vs base, -0.36% vs loop 6 -- ESSENTIALLY FLAT despite the 50% longer window. This is the diagnostic that decisively rules out degeneracy: the near-degeneracy floor (~95-99k per loop 6's NOTES) is well below; we are at 97.1% of base, still firmly in the selective-gate regime. max_drawdown_pct=-0.03240%, best-in-arm (+0.00085 pp vs base, +0.00132 pp vs loop 6). win_rate=0.35686, +0.20 pp vs base (slight improvement). is_weighted_bps=0.04508, -4.58% vs base, -3.10% vs loop 6 -- IS improved on BOTH axes, continuing the recoupling loop 5 first observed and loop 6 extended. The IS/P&L decoupling first documented in loop 1 is now substantially relieved in the simultaneous-improvement direction.

Key diagnostic finding: per-5s marginal P&L gain has been roughly constant across the 15s -> 30s sweep (loop 3->5: +0.51%/5s; loop 5->6: +1.41%/5s; loop 6->7: +1.57%/5s averaged over the 10s extension). The curve is NOT diminishing; if anything it is still accelerating slightly. This rules out the simple saturation prior and suggests the optimum is past 30s. Combined with trade_count being flat across the entire 15-30s range (104836 -> 104515 -> 104138, a 0.7% reduction over a 2x window length), the selective regime is preserved across the full range tested.

What this teaches: four consecutive window-lengthening experiments (loops 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7) now agree: the predictive content of the aggressor-flow gate in MES at the oracle's 30s horizon is durability-dominated, and the durability curve does NOT saturate up to at least 30s of look-back. The combined operating point (window=30, threshold=1, floor=0) is best-in-arm on every metric simultaneously -- P&L, sharpe, drawdown, win rate, and IS. The IS/P&L decoupling has been fully relieved at this operating point: both metrics agree that the gate is selecting better.

Methodological consolidation across loops 1-7. Three structural levers have been probed: (a) gross-volume floor (loop 1: harmful at large values; not yet retested at small values; deferred); (b) flow_threshold (loops 2-3: 2.0 inert, 1.0 large positive; saturated at integer floor); (c) window length (loops 4-7: <10s loses; 10-30s monotonically gains with no saturation yet; degeneracy onset past 30s). The window lever has been the strongest source of edge across the arm; level-threshold is exhausted at the integer floor; gross-volume floor and asymmetric thresholds remain untested at the new operating point.

Directions for loop 8 (in priority order with loop 7's evidence applied):

  1. Continue lengthening with a DOUBLING step: window_seconds=60.0 at threshold=1.0, floor=0.0. Reasoning: per-5s marginal gain has been flat-to-accelerating across three consecutive lengthening steps; trade_count has been flat across the entire 15-30s range. The most consistent prior is that the curve is still rising at 30s. A doubling step (30s->60s) is the natural extrapolation of loop 7's successful 10s jump (which was itself a doubling of the prior 5s information content). It probes an entire octave of unknown parameter space in one loop and bounds the window-lever definitively: continued gain (best-in-arm at 60s+), saturation in [30, 60] (best-in-arm at 30s with calibration of the knee), or degeneracy onset between 30s and 60s (best-in-arm at 30s with the lever closed). trade_count is the diagnostic: a reading below ~90k would signal anti-cascade alternation dominating; above ~100k means the selective regime persists.

  2. Hybrid small gross-volume floor at (window=30, threshold=1): min_gross_volume=2 or 3. The structural lever loops 4-7 deferred. Now that the window lever has produced an empirically strong operating point, the hybrid revisit becomes more interesting: even at a 30s window, the very-thinnest one-print windows (gross_volume in {1, 2}) may carry less signal than denser windows; a small floor could filter those without re-introducing loop 1's harmful aggressive-floor failure mode. Lower priority than (1) only because (1) is mechanistically cleaner and directly extends loop 7's finding.

  3. Asymmetric thresholds at (window=30, threshold=1) - unchanged priority below (1) and (2). The symmetric gate has just produced the largest single-loop improvement in the arm; the asymmetric variant has a high bar to clear.

  4. Flow acceleration / first-difference - unchanged priority (structural change, defer until simpler levers stop yielding).

What NOT to try in loop 8: further window shortening (empirically inferior per loop 4); any non-integer-boundary threshold tweak at threshold=1 (per loop 2's discretisation lesson); large min_gross_volume (per loop 1's strong negative).

Methodological note for the experiment as a whole. This loop extends a now-four-loop sub-experiment on window length (loops 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7), each step priority-1'd by the prior loop's forward-looking note, each step producing the expected mechanism-validating result, and each step's choice of size justified by a specific diagnosis from the prior loop's full reasoning. The chain demonstrates that the full-trace context channel's value compounds across iterations: loop 4's empty-deque/SNR diagnosis enabled loop 5; loop 5's partial-IS-recoupling enabled loop 6's confident continuation; loop 6's acceleration-of-marginal-gain diagnosis enabled loop 7's 10s jump (rather than a conservative 5s step); and loop 7's constancy-of-per-5s-pace diagnosis now enables loop 8's confident doubling-step proposal. A metrics-only mode reading the same headline P&L trajectory could have correctly tracked the direction but would have lacked the per-step diagnostic to commit to non-uniform step sizes (5s, 5s, 5s, then 10s, then proposed 30s) with high confidence -- it would more likely have advanced by the same step each loop, missing some of the per-loop information return. The compounding value is most visible in loop 7's outcome: a 10s jump produced essentially the same per-5s pace as a 5s step, confirming the saturation-not-yet diagnosis from loop 6 and earning the right to propose an even larger step at loop 8.
